title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is upside down in the scan. It is not Grothendieck's motivic material. It is a page (p. 9, Bourbaki redaction n°370) of a typescript draft of Bourbaki, Intégration, Chap. VII, §1 (Haar measure). It was presumably reused as scrap paper, with the 'Théorie de Galois des motifs' notes on the other side; the neighbouring pages are handwritten notes on fibre functors ξ_v for complex embeddings and motivic Galois torsors.

The content is the end of the uniqueness proof for Haar measure. One has a left Haar measure μ and a left-invariant measure ν, and for each f a function D_f with formula (14). The argument runs as follows:
- For f, f' with μ(f), μ(f') ≠ 0, one has μ((D_f − D_{f'})g) = 0 for all g ∈ K(G).
- Replacing g by (D_f − D_{f'})ḡ gives μ(|D_f − D_{f'}|² g) = 0 for all g ≥ 0.
- Since supp μ = G, this forces D_f = D_{f'} =: D.
- Then (14) gives μ(f)D(e) = ν̌(f) (17). By linearity this extends to f with μ(f) = 0.
- D(e) ≠ 0 because ν̌ ≠ 0. Hence μ and ν̌ are proportional.

Corollary: every complex left- (resp. right-) invariant measure is proportional to a left (resp. right) Haar measure.

Examples:
1. Lebesgue measure on ℝ.
2. dx/x on ℝ₊*, verified by the change of variables x ↦ tx.
3. On 𝕋 = ℝ/ℤ, the measure I(f) = ∫_a^{a+1} f(φ(x)) dx, which is independent of a and translation-invariant. Transporting it gives Haar measure on 𝕌 via t ↦ e^{2πit}.

The page then begins Proposition 1: G is discrete iff μ({e}) > 0 (the statement is cut off). All of this is standard textbook material serving Bourbaki's exposition of Haar measure.
